content.summary: The exact outsider census has precisely the four claimed admissible count triples after the nine-completion and I27 restrictions. Detailed diagnostic bitmasks reconcile with their aggregate histogram, and newly frozen SAT output confirms UNKNOWN. These checks support recorded calculations and disclosures without promoting exploratory45 to a theorem.

checks.scope: Profile A count window and rounding robustness
checks.method: Enumerated nonnegative integer solutions to n0+n1+n2=61 and n1+2n2=76 with n0>=9,n2<=27; separately evaluated the meeting inequality for every possible outsider count0,...,4.
checks.observation: Exactly four triples remain: (9,28,24),(10,26,25),(11,24,26),(12,22,27). Degree sums56+5i give meeting caps47,49,52,54,57 and hence at least14,12,9,7,4 disjoint members respectively. In particular the generic disjoint-existence claim and the nine-completion bound at i=2 have correct integer rounding. This is a fresh finite calculation; the unchanged overlap and weighted-pair checks from round3 were reused.

checks.scope: Detailed exploratory-output consistency and unsuccessful solver provenance
checks.method: Checked all22 nonempty rows of the frozen Python diagnostic: candidate uniqueness/count, bit population, support-union containment and intersection sizes; aggregated support-intersection histograms. Read and hash-checked the newly frozen SAT files against their manifest.
checks.observation: All listed candidates are four-sets in the actual link union;22 rows comprise10 with3 candidates,10 with1 and2 with5, totaling50 candidate occurrences. Their aggregated histogram equals both reported global histograms. The SAT output explicitly records UNKNOWN, and the log states a120-second limit; encoding metadata openly omits all zero-high/three-low sunflower exclusions. This supports the non-result disclosure only and does not prove a complete geometry normalization, universal45 or SAT infeasibility.
